title: At which level do the differences of cubes become the same?
description: Differences are taken again and again from the cubes one, eight, twenty seven and so on, until they stop changing. Keeko doubts the level, because the differences of squares became the same one level earlier.
teaching_notes: One idea: take differences level after level until a whole level is the same number. Watch for students who expect cubes to settle at the same level as squares.

source: Find the successive differences of the cubes 1, 8, 27, 64, 125 and 216 until they are constant.
video_script.why: The child takes differences of the cubes level after level and sees that they become constant at level three, one level later than squares.
video_script.substitution: Subtract each number from the next to make a new row, and repeat until a row has one repeated number.
video_script.anchor: a row of perfect squares and a row of perfect cubes, side by side
video_script.wrong_answer: the differences of cubes become the same at level two
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko expects cubes to behave like squares, whose differences become the same at level two. The second row for cubes is twelve, eighteen, twenty four and thirty, so another level is needed.
video_script.payoff_line: The differences are all six at level three

final_answer.spoken: the differences are all six at level three

maths_rules: check: next level 3 is 6, level 2 is 30 + 6 = 36, level 1 is 91 + 36 = 127, next cube is 216 + 127 = 343 = 7³
video_script.design: One idea: repeat the differences until a level is constant. Wrong idea: cubes settle at the same level as squares. The two rows sit in the anchor band and the levels build on the working board.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='sq'/>For the squares, the differences are three, five, seven and nine.
<bookmark mark='same'/>The differences of those are all two.
<bookmark mark='cubes'/>The cubes begin with one, eight, twenty seven and sixty four.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>At which level do their differences become the same, and what is that number?

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Think and tell.

narration: <bookmark mark='sub'/>To find the differences of a row, we subtract each number from the next one.
<bookmark mark='level'/>The new row is the next level.
<bookmark mark='stop'/>We keep going until all the numbers in a level are the same.

marks.given: the six cubes are written in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the cubes one, eight, twenty seven, sixty four, one hundred twenty five and two hundred sixteen.

beats.on_screen: To find: the level where all the differences are the same

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the level where all the differences are the same.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, subtract each cube from the next. Eight minus one is seven, and twenty seven minus eight is nineteen.
<bookmark mark='third'/>Sixty four minus twenty seven is thirty seven.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The next two are sixty one and ninety one.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Step two, subtract again. Nineteen minus seven is twelve, and thirty seven minus nineteen is eighteen.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Sixty one minus thirty seven is twenty four, and ninety one minus sixty one is thirty.

marks.rest: 30 − 24 = 6 is written and the three 6s are circled

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step three, subtract once more. Eighteen minus twelve is six, and twenty four minus eighteen is six.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Thirty minus twenty four is also six, so this whole level is the same.

beats.on_screen: check by building up: level 3 gives 6, level 2 gets 30 + 6 = 36, level 1 gets 91 + 36 = 127, next cube 216 + 127 = 343 = 7³

marks.back: the words build the next cube from the 6 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step four, check by building up the next cube from the six.
<bookmark mark='up'/>Thirty plus six is thirty six, and ninety one plus thirty six is one hundred twenty seven.
<bookmark mark='cube'/>Two hundred sixteen plus one hundred twenty seven is three hundred forty three, which is seven cubed.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The differences are all six at level three.
Squares settled after two levels, and cubes need one more.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble says level 2 is the same; the cube row at level 2, 12, 18, 24, 30, is shown with the values changing, and the bubble is struck through

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble appears with level 2 inside
marks.row: the level 2 row of cubes, 12, 18, 24, 30, appears with arrows showing it still grows
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour and a third level appears

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the differences of cubes become the same at level two, as they did for squares.
<bookmark mark='row'/>But the second row is twelve, eighteen, twenty four and thirty, and these keep growing.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Cubes need one more level before the numbers match.
